records.title: Combining search results in PostgreSQL
records.summary: A small SQL experiment with filtered nearest neighbours, text matches and reciprocal rank fusion, including the results that disappear when LIMIT comes too early.
records.name_tokens: combining search results in postgresql others postgresql sql hybrid search vector search full text search pgvector ranking
records.text_tokens: a small sql experiment with filtered nearest neighbours text matches and reciprocal rank fusion including the results that disappear when limit comes too early suppose i have a table of specimen notes and want to find something about a failed library preparation some notes use exactly those words while others describe the same problem as “too little material after amplification” i would like both to appear but only if they belong to the study i am currently looking at there are two separate decisions here which rows are allowed into the answer and how to order those rows keeping them separate makes it much easier to explain why a search returned something odd especially when more than one search method contributes results the term hybrid search is used for both combining lexical and semantic retrieval and combining vector retrieval with ordinary filters i want to look at the boundary between these two uses with a deliberately small sql experiment the numbers below are invented distances and ranks so the examples require postgresql but no embedding model or additional extension losing a row before the search is finished here are four notes already assigned distances from a query smaller means closer only study a is relevant to the request and i want two results with notes id study distance as values 11 b 0 04 12 a 0 08 13 b 0 10 14 a 0 16 nearest as select from notes order by distance id limit 2 filtered first as select from notes where study a order by distance id limit 2 select limit then filter as approach array agg id order by distance id as ids from nearest where study a union all select filter then limit array agg id order by distance id from filtered first the first answer contains only note 12 note 14 never gets a chance because the inner query has already discarded it increasing the final limit cannot bring it back this is a consequence of where i put the limit even with perfectly accurate distances and no index involved the id is a tie breaker which makes the example reproducible if two distances become equal postgresql does not promise which tied rows a limited query will choose unless the ordering distinguishes them that matters for tests and for a reader trying the example twice postgresql s limit documentation describes this behaviour where an approximate index changes the problem with pgvector an approximate index can find nearby candidates without comparing the query against every stored embedding filters are applied to those candidates which means a restrictive study filter can leave fewer results than requested iterative scans available since pgvector 0 8 0 can continue looking but scan limits still matter an ordered result also does not prove that every closer eligible row was found pgvector documents both filtering and iterative scans for a small eligible subset i would first measure an exact distance sort after filtering then compare an approximate plan against that answer there is no universal row count at which one becomes better the distance calculation the distribution of studies and the amount of data all enter the measurement having an index on the study column and another on embeddings does not by itself settle that choice postgresql can combine suitable index scans through bitmaps but the bitmap represents matching table locations and loses the original index ordering an ordered nearest neighbour search needs more than a set of matching locations combining multiple indexes explains the bitmap part combining two ranked lists now suppose the eligible notes have been searched twice a lexical search found note 21 first while the embedding search preferred note 24 postgresql s built in text search can produce the lexical matches and a relevance ranking its scores describe that ranking method not a probability that a note answers the question the text search documentation explains the available ranking functions i do not want to add a text score directly to a vector distance their scales and directions have different meanings for this experiment i use reciprocal rank fusion instead adding 1 60 position for each list containing a note a missing note contributes nothing the constant 60 comes from the original rrf paper it is a choice to evaluate not a property of postgresql cormack clarke and buettcher 2009 with lexical note id position as values 21 1 24 2 28 3 semantic note id position as values 24 1 31 2 21 3 contributions as select note id 1 0 60 position as weight from lexical union all select note id 1 0 60 position from semantic select note id round sum weight 6 as fused score from contributions group by note id order by sum weight desc note id note 24 wins because it appears near the top of both lists note 31 still appears even though the lexical search did not find it union all is intentional each list provides its own contribution within each input list however a note must occur only once otherwise joins that duplicate rows would accidentally give it extra votes this is a useful place to stop and inspect the candidates fusion cannot recover a note absent from both lists and asking each method for only two candidates may remove a note that would have done well in the combined ranking i would choose candidate limits separately from the number of results displayed to the reader what i would measure for each test query i would keep the eligible ids each candidate list and the final ordering together with the query time this makes a missing result traceable was it excluded by the study filter absent from retrieval or just ranked too low a single response time number cannot answer that i would also include awkward cases a rare study a note containing an exact sample identifier two notes with tied scores and a query with no lexical match the occasional empty answer is less suprising when those cases are part of the test data from the beginning the tiny datasets here are a way to inspect the decisions in sql before choosing an index or a larger retrieval setup

point at a row and explain why it belongs in the result a search box which returns something plausible is a useful beginning but it becomes less convincing when a slightly different phrase makes a specimen disappear and the only explanation is somewhere inside an orm generated query for this example i use a few invented laboratory notes and a deliberately small rule include a note if it contains the phrase “low coverage” or if it contains both “repeat” and “extraction” this gives me something concrete to check before adding a search scope a ranking formula or another index here pg search means the rails gem the examples below use postgresql 17 s built in text search they do not require the separate postgresql extension also named pg search decide what a match means i would not make visitors type postgresql s query syntax into an ordinary search box for free form input websearch to tsquery understands quoted phrases or and exclusion with a minus sign a field which promises a phrase has a narrower job so phraseto tsquery fits it better these are different input contracts even when their ui is just a text field postgresql documents the query parsers and their syntax select phraseto tsquery english low coverage as phrase websearch to tsquery english repeat extraction as words once input has become a tsquery i can combine values using the query operators there is no need to build a new query language by replacing spaces with operator characters and doing so would make punctuation surprisingly important keep a searchable document beside the note a tsvector stores normalized lexemes and can keep their positions it is not the original text and it is not a numeric embedding stemming can change a word and a dictionary can remove it altogether that is why i keep tsvector generated always as to tsvector english regconfig note stored create index specimen notes search on specimen notes using gin search document the explicit configuration makes the choice of dictionary visible in the schema a stored generated column also means that changing note updates its search document including when the write comes from somewhere outside rails it costs storage and work on writes so i would measure that cost on a realistic collection before treating it as free the gin index can help find matching documents it does not sort them by my application s preferred order and a three row example says very little about performance a sequential scan here is perfectly reasonable i would check the plan again after loading enough notes to represent the actual workload return the reason along with the row the rows are made up for this query one mentions low coverage one recommends repeating an extraction and one records a routine check with rules as select phraseto tsquery english low coverage as coverage plainto tsquery english repeat extraction as retry select specimen search document coverage as coverage match search document retry as retry match from specimen notes cross join rules where search document coverage retry order by id the result tells me which branch accepted each note which is more useful while debugging than a single unexplained score i would keep examples where only one requested word appears where the phrase is reversed and where the input is empty because those cases pin down what the interface actually promises phrase matching follows normalized lexemes and positions so it is not a byte for byte substring test if i need to find an exact accession identifier i would use a seperate identifier column and ordinary equality rather than hope the language dictionary preserves it use the stored document from rails for an ordinary all words scope the pg search gem can use the stored column class specimennote applicationrecord include pgsearch model pg search scope search notes against note using tsearch dictionary english tsvector column search document end this scope is an integration example not an implementation of the two branch rule above for that rule i would keep the sql explicit and bind the inputs rails query parameter guidance matters here parsing search text is different from safely passing that text to sql an input string still belongs in a parameter not inside an interpolated sql expression the harder maintenance question appears when a search document includes another table a generated column cannot reach across rows to follow an association so i would first decide which change owns the refresh then test updates to both the parent and the child searching stale text is a correctness problem even if the index makes it very quick finally a highlighted excerpt is presentation not proof of a match ts headline needs the original text and its output is not automatically safe html the highlighting documentation explains the limitations i would keep the matching booleans for debugging and render excerpts through the application s escaping or sanitizing rules rather than marking arbitrary output as safe

records.title: What PostgreSQL encryption at rest actually protects
records.summary: Follow a specimen record from a SQL query to an encrypted file, and see where pg_tde, key management, WAL and backups fit into the picture.
records.name_tokens: what postgresql encryption at rest actually protects others postgresql encryption pg tde database security wal backups key management
records.text_tokens: follow a specimen record from a sql query to an encrypted file and see where pg tde key management wal and backups fit into the picture suppose i keep specimen identifiers and laboratory notes in postgresql a copy of the database directory ends up on a misplaced disk while the database itself is still running somewhere else i want the copied files to be unreadable but i also want the application to carry on using ordinary select statements without adding a decryption call to every query that is the useful part of transparent data encryption or tde the word “transparent” describes the application s view storage can change while sql still returns the original values it does not mean those values stop being sensitive once the server has read them follow the record then choose the boundary an authorised database session needs readable rows to filter and return results encrypting stored files therefore does not stop that session from reading a specimen note nor does it conceal the note from a fully compromised running server the connection needs its own protection normally tls and database permissions still decide who can issue the query postgresql describes these separate layers in its encryption options i find it easier to draw this boundary before choosing an extension because “the database is encrypted” says very little about a csv export sitting beside it an application log containing query results or the person holding a database password where pg tde fits this example refers to pg tde 2 2 2 using its documented configuration as of october 2026 it requires the changes in percona server for postgresql installing the extension package into an arbitrary community postgresql build is not an equivalent setup the supported deployment list covers percona server 17 5 and later while the postgresql 16 build is a technology preview this is a general postgresql example it does not establish compatibility with bioseqdb s own table access method for a table created with using tde heap the extension covers its stored data indexes and associated toast data toast matters here because a long specimen note may live outside the main table s pages column names and other table metadata remain visible see the documented encrypted data scope there is another distinction which is easy to miss a temporary table and a temporary file produced by a large sort are different things version 2 2 2 leaves query spill files and postgresql s system catalogues unencrypted including statistics those are meaningful limits when the aim is to protect patient information so disk protection may still have a separate job to do the limitations page is part of the design not something to read after deployment a small check before configuring encryption the query below inspects an ordinary heap table containing two invented records it is run by this website s postgresql test database which does not have pg tde installed its result demonstrates how to inspect a table s access method it is not an encryption test select c relname as table name a amname as access method select count from specimen notes as records from pg class as c join pg am as a on a oid c relam where c oid specimen notes regclass on the encryption side the principal key protects internal keys and those internal keys protect the stored files keeping the principal key in an external key service separates it from the files it unlocks a copied database directory should not arrive with everything needed to decrypt it the architecture description explains this hierarchy the following is optional administrative sql for pg tde 2 2 2 not executed by this website it assumes pg tde is installed and preloaded the extension has been created in this database and an administrator has configured a database key provider named specimen kms provider credentials and service configuration belong outside this example select pg tde create key using database key provider specimen key 2026 specimen kms select pg tde set key using database key provider specimen key 2026 specimen kms create table encrypted specimen notes specimen id integer primary key patient code text not null note text not null using tde heap select pg tde is encrypted encrypted specimen notes these calls follow the function reference they do not encrypt the earlier specimen notes table merely because another table now uses tde a local file provider can help with a disposable experiment but its key file is unencrypted the keyring guide recommends proper key management for production wal and recovery need their own plan table encryption alone does not settle the write ahead log wal encryption became generally available in pg tde 2 0 after some early introductions were written it has a separate server wide configuration covers writes from all databases in the cluster and needs a restart when enabled existing plaintext wal does not become encrypted retrospectively follow the current wal instructions including their required archive and restore wrappers a logical dump is another copy of readable data pg dump reads through postgresql s client interface rather than preserving encrypted relation files protect the resulting dump separately the sql dump documentation explains that distinction in how the backup is made for physical backups i would make recovery the acceptance test restore elsewhere recover the required keys replay wal and check the specimen rows percona s backup procedure specifies the encryption metadata and provider files needed and warns against rotating keys during a backup it is a seperate operational dependency worth rehearsing before there is an incident

records.title: What does vector mean in PostgreSQL?
records.summary: Text-search vectors, embeddings, arrays, geometric points and execution batches share a word but have different jobs. A few small SQL queries help tell them apart.
records.name_tokens: what does vector mean in postgresql others postgresql sql vector tsvector pgvector arrays vectorized execution
records.text_tokens: text search vectors embeddings arrays geometric points and execution batches share a word but have different jobs a few small sql queries help tell them apart if a database feature says it supports vectors i still need to ask what i can put into it and which operations it supports a vector might be a value stored in one row a collection of values being processed together or the outline of an illustration on this page those uses can appear in the same application without sharing an implementation i find it easier to start with a sample record than with the word itself imagine a specimen with a free text note three measurements and a position on a laboratory diagram all three belong to the sample but searching the note comparing measurements and drawing its position are separate tasks the vector made of words postgresql s tsvector stores lexemes which are the normalized terms used by full text search with optional positions and weights it is not a list of embedding coordinates i can inspect the difference using a note that mentions the same thing twice with note as select to tsvector english samples were frozen the second sample thawed as terms select terms terms plainto tsquery english frozen sample as matches from note the rendered value is organized by lexeme so it no longer looks like the original sentence positions preserve information about where terms occurred a tsquery supplies the search condition and tests whether the document representation matches it there is no embedding model hidden inside this query text search types and text search operators describe the two types and their relationship for these examples i name the english configuration explicitly a sample identifier is a different problem from ordinary english prose and i would inspect its tokenization before deciding to feed it through the same configuration in particular turning a note into searchable terms is not a reversible way to store the note itself i would keep the original text as well a list of numbers still needs a meaning three measurements fit in a postgresql array although their interpretation remains part of the schema and the application here i have arranged them in the order concentration volume and temperature the database cannot infer those labels from the array with sample measurements as values array 12 5 40 0 4 0 real select measurements 1 as concentration measurements 2 as volume measurements 3 as temperature cardinality measurements as dimensions from sample writing an array declaration with a size such as real 3 does not enforce that size in postgresql if i need exactly three entries i must enforce that separately and array bounds deserve attention too if values can arrive from outside the application the array documentation covers these details even when two arrays have the same length blindly computing their distance might be meaningless a change of one degree and a change of one microlitre are different quantities converting just one measurement to another unit would change the numerical distance that is a modelling decision not something an index can fix an embedding also contains numbers but its coordinates come from a chosen representation of the input pgvector supplies a vector type and distance operators for this use the following optional example requires the separately installed pgvector extension it uses invented coordinates rather than real specimen embeddings create extension if not exists vector select 0 2 0 4 0 6 vector 3 0 2 0 4 0 9 vector 3 as distance here means euclidean distance for those operand types choosing a distance and generating comparable inputs remain separate from storing the values the pgvector reference lists the supported operators in an actual experiment i would record the embedding model and preprocessing alongside the data so a later model change cannot quietly mix incompatible representations the same operator can describe a different distance a point on a two dimensional laboratory drawing does not need an embedding extension postgresql already has geometric types including point and the point to point distance operator is also written select point 2 3 as storage position point 5 7 as workbench position point 2 3 point 5 7 as drawing distance this returns a distance of five drawing units the type tells postgresql which operation to perform even though the operator spelling is shared with the previous example these built in coordinates describe a plane they do not carry a geographic coordinate reference system geometric types and their operators specify the available operations vector graphics add another use of the word the illustration above consists of shapes and text while an svg path can describe a shape through drawing commands and coordinates the browser paints that description at the requested size those coordinates are instructions for an image not a search representation of its meaning the svg path specification explains that format a vector can also span many rows vectorized execution refers to how a database processes data internally for example duckdb s execution format passes batches of values through operators and a batch can contain ordinary integers or strings its documentation distinguishes several physical representations including flat and constant vectors the sql column does not have to contain embeddings for this execution method to be useful duckdb describes these representations in its execution format documentation that distinction prevents an occassional misunderstanding adding a vector column to a postgresql table does not by itself turn the query executor into a batch processing engine a stored value s type and the way an executor moves through rows answer different questions when reading about a vector feature i therefore try to identify the stored value the operation and the execution method separately for the specimen example those questions lead to fairly ordinary choices retain the note define the measurements name the coordinate system and test the search behaviour the shared vocabulary becomes much less troublesome once those choices are written down

usually start with the query and its indexes because those are the parts i can change without asking awkward questions about where the rows actually live postgresql also has a place to change that last part a table access method for this post i wanted to start with an ordinary table and a question i can answer from sql which part owns its storage and which part helps me find a row two meanings amname a table method manages the table s rows an index method manages an index choosing a b tree for a specimen identifier does not turn the underlying table into a b tree table and dropping that index does not discard the specimen records i find that distinction easier to remember when i inspect both objects together follow one table here is the small table i use below the specimens are invented and the counts are just values which make the output easy to check create table lab observations specimen text primary key read count integer not null needs review boolean not null using heap create index lab observations count idx on lab observations using btree read count heap is postgresql s default table access method i spell it out so the example does not depend on a changed session default the method actually attached to a relation is recorded in pg class relam so i can join that value back to the catalog above select relation relname as object name method amname as access method from pg class as relation join pg am as method on method oid relation relam where relation oid in lab observations regclass lab observations count idx regclass order by object name there are two objects here with two different jobs even though they describe the same collection of observations that gives me a useful boundary for an experiment i can ask whether i need a different way to locate candidates or whether i really need a different representation of the table itself returning a row is the beginning a table access method supplies a handler returning a tableamroutine whose callbacks let postgresql request operations such as starting a scan or inserting a tuple a tuple slot provides a representation of a row that the rest of the executor can use without understanding every detail of its storage the table access method documentation describes that interface and the constraints around row identifiers this is an attractive place to experiment but the first successful select answers a very small question if i put three records into an array and read them back i have demonstrated that particular path through my code i have not established what happens when a second connection arrives a transaction aborts or the server disappears halfway through a write for example mvcc gives a query a view of the database through a snapshot “return the newest record i can find” is not enough when that record belongs to a transaction the reader cannot see i would test an uncommitted update from another connection before spending time comparing scan speeds an index lookup has the same visibility problem the table method s index fetch tuple callback receives a candidate identifier and a snapshot it must find a suitable visible tuple rather than blindly trust the index entry the api comments also distinguish ordinary vacuum work from the callbacks used by analyze and table rewrites these are different operations even when they all involve visiting stored data keep an ordinary query as a reference i would keep this kind of deliberately boring query beside a storage experiment select specimen read count from lab observations where needs review order by read count desc specimen the expected result is small enough to check by eye from there i would add updates rollbacks deleted rows and overlapping readers keeping the expected answers seperate from the engine s implementation a faster result is useful only after i know it is the right result reclaiming obsolete data also needs attention postgresql s heap requires routine vacuuming a different storage design still needs a clear account of when old information can be removed i would include a long running reader in that experiment because reclaiming something too early is harder to notice than retaining it too long the part that survives a restart write ahead logging provides the ordering needed to recover logged changes after a crash a custom method needs its own coherent recovery story postgresql s table interface permits its wal facilities or another implementation an in memory demonstration should not be mistaken for durable storage just because it accepts familiar sql there is an operational boundary too in postgresql 17 changing an existing table with alter table set access method rewrites it and requires an access exclusive lock i would plan that as a migration with room for the rewrite and a tested way back rather than treat it as an inexpensive setting the version specific alter table documentation is the place to check before doing it what interests me here is the amount of postgresql i can keep while investigating a different storage layout the sql examples above deliberately stay with heap they establish the boundary and a few expected results leaving the larger implementation questions visible instead of hiding them behind a successful demo
